ets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, bec
ause cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went sil

ent
 and the watchdog settled the run.
* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can
 resolve to

the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
 targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **sp
ends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`\n> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst brake\n>
(retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on y

our own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll-up and the score

card are deterministic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What

it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |
| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` |
Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `PO
ST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's gene
rated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled, not don

e |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming,

because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.**

Three failures
 out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
 7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is

not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
 regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.

And one
modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —\n`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.
\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismissed, and hiding one never claims it sto

pped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJam. It s
till counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insight
s, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a

second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (wait seconds), a `429` nam
ing `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the fe
ature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help.\n\n**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{e
nvironmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`) — publishing an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling w

ho can reach it. A **study** is a published
environment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoi
nt | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns th
e existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpubli
sh.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` |
Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with fee
dback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool pa
yloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credi
ts, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secr
et is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` stu
dy |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessi

ons |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
\n> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants
already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you rea
ch for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have

.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, an
d removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None

of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion

` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did*
* — the analytics reads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\ndeterministic an

d free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volu
mes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{stu
dyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../s
tudies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{s
tudyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowI
d}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{stu
dyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not
been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |
\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed w

hen insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response inc
ludes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncov
erage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments`
distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map independently. Readin

g this response never starts analysis.

Taxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme ids
remain sta
ble across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired
or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version provenance, not

historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope tot
al. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover onl

y its requested
goal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.
